steps.step: Boot 2: DB init + restore_state gate the watcher
steps.what: run.py:45-99 runs Database.init(), exits 3 on bad DATABASE_URL, runs restore_state() (guards fail-closed until all loaders succeed, state_restore.py:60-74), exits 1 on failure — and only THEN starts the watcher task (run.py:104-111).

A DB-down loop costs forward samples in the canonical dataset for free.

steps.step: Block cursor init: head+1, forward-only, not persisted
steps.what: Cursor starts at current head+1 at every boot (copy_watcher.py:552); no backfill, no cursor persistence; per-window advance only after success or loud skip (:606-612, :690-691).
steps.why_money_logic: Forward-only matches the instrument's purpose (generate the missing FORWARD fill-quality dataset, :9-13) and the operator's FORWARD-DATA-ONLY rule (docs/MB_STATE.md:769-779): backfilled blocks could not have been copied live, so including them would flatter latency/fill stats. Not persisting the cursor keeps restarts simple at the cost of dropping every block between crash and reboot.
steps.works_detail: Logic traced. The restart gap is a real, unmeasured sample-loss channel that sits oddly beside the retry-don't-skip machinery built to never lose a window (:587-592) — the code fights window loss hard intra-process and accepts it silently across restarts.

steps.verify_note: Verified: :552 head+1 at every boot; no cursor persistence anywhere in the module; advance only on success (:612) or loud skip (:607) with retry reset (:609); closing comment :690-691. Restart-gap observation accurate.

steps.what: A failed window is retried from the same cursor next poll; MAX_WINDOW_RETRIES=5 consecutive failures -> LOUD skip and advance (copy_watcher.py:79, :586-612).

Bounded retries prevent the opposite failure (permanent stall on a poisoned window). ~10s worst case before a loud skip is a sane trade.
steps.works_detail: Traced both branches: retry resets cursor=lo and breaks (window recomputed next poll); skip logs the dropped range explicitly, resets fail_streak, advances. fail_streak resets on any success so it effectively tracks one window.

steps.what: Fills sharing (tx, trader, token) merge into one wager: USD summed, price volume-weighted (sizing.py:120-140), applied per window (copy_watcher.py:613-623).
steps.why_money_logic: One whale order lands as several fills; taking the first clip alone under-reads stake and mis-prices conviction r — which would corrupt the very field the sizing hypothesis will be judged on. VWAP price is the correct whale entry for the chase gate.
steps.works_detail: Window-boundary safety is structural: a tx cannot span blocks and chunks split on block boundaries, so all fills of one tx always land in one window — merge never splits. Known semantic limit (shared with the cache seeder, so the estimator is consistent): a resting order filled across multiple txs counts as multiple wagers.

steps.what: get_block(sig._block) under rpc_call for block_ts; on ANY failure block_ts=int(now) (copy_watcher.py:644-648); detect_lag_s = now - block_ts recorded (:403).
steps.why_money_logic: block_ts is the denominator of the latency measurement — detect_lag_s is a headline stat for the chain-vs-RTDS source decision. The fallback exists so a timestamp hiccup never costs the record itself.
steps.works_detail: The fallback silently writes detect_lag_s≈0 with no marker distinguishing measured from fabricated. Failure scenario: a flaky RPC afternoon makes get_block fail on 5% of signals -> the lag distribution grows a spurious spike at ~0s -> p50/p90 lag understated -> the latency case for/against the RTDS source swap is distorted in the fast direction. The record should carry block_ts=null or a fallback flag; the why (keep the record) is right, the silent impersonation of a measurement is not.
steps.measurement_needed: Metric: count of sink records with detect_lag_s in [-0.5, 0.5] (physically implausible for a 2s poll + block time) vs total — existing mirror3_shadow.jsonl quantifies how much of the lag dataset is fabricated today.

Failure scenario (spurious ~0s spike understating p50/p90 lag under RPC flakiness) is mechanically accurate. Real measurement-integrity gap, not a false accusation.

steps.what: In-memory set of (trader, token); first BUY flagged first_buy=True, repeats recorded but flagged False (copy_watcher.py:444-457, :650-651). No persistence.
steps.evidence: copy_watcher.py:444-457, :650-651; consumers: scripts/mb_canon.py:69, scripts/band_tracker.py:59 (filter on first_buy AND verdict==OK)
steps.why_money_logic: The walk-forward's graded estimand is FIRST buy per (trader, token) — the one signal MB's one-bet-per-market guard could actually take. Flagging instead of dropping keeps repeats available for other analyses without contaminating the estimand.
steps.works_detail: The flag implements per-PROCESS first, not per-HISTORY first: _seen dies with the process, and canonical readouts consume the flag as-is (mb_canon.py:69, band_tracker.py:59). Failure scenario: service restarts at T; a rostered trader who bought token X last week adds to the position at T+1h; the record is stamped first_buy=True and enters the canon estimand as a first buy — later adds systematically have different price dynamics than true firsts, so every restart injects estimand contamination. Note the bidsim registry solved this exact problem for itself with sink rehydration (:1057-1098); the estimand flag did not get the same fix.
steps.measurement_needed: Metric: fraction of first_buy=True sink records that are NOT globally first = group full mirror3_shadow.jsonl by (trader, token_id), min detect_ts wins, count flagged-first records that lose. Pure existing-data computation; also yields the corrected estimand set readouts should use.

steps.step: 13. THE DEADLOCK: paper-engine directional adverse-slippage guard vs its own force-exit SELL
steps.what: MB submits SELL at stale anchor (Step 11). order_gateway walks the REAL bid book and passes VWAP via event_data (order_gateway.py:1013-1030 _vwap_from_bids, :1118-1130 _shadow_* passthrough). Paper engine sets fill price to that VWAP (paper_trading.py:513-521), then the guard: adverse = original_price - price for SELL; if book-walk used and adverse >= 0.5c and adverse/original > 10% (20% for anchors <0.20) -> reject with fail_code='slippage' (paper_trading.py:560-574; FAIL_SLIPPAGE :21). original_price = caller anchor unless BOTH gamma-index bid AND ask were found (paper_trading.py:456-463; gateway lookup order_gateway.py:1142-1168 — misses for markets fallen out of the scan index, i.e. old positions). MB classifies 'slippage' (:1865-1866), backs off 100->200->400s cap 900s after 3 fails (:1810-1817), and retries the identical stale-anchored order forever. Observed live: 678h / 28 days, basis 0.68 vs market 0.31 = 54.4% (MB_OVERHAUL_REVIEW_AGENDA.md:27-32).
steps.why_money_logic: The guard's legitimate why is ENTRY protection: don't model a paper BUY filling deep through a thin book at a price no live limit order would accept — that would flatter paper P&L. Applied to a risk-REDUCING forced SELL it inverts into money-destruction: it converts a stale mark into a permanent refusal to realize a real loss, freezing capital, a cap slot, and the market's one-bet-per-market lane, while the loss keeps floating unbooked. There is no money-logic under which 'refuse to liquidate because the market is far below our stale mark' helps the bot.
steps.works_detail: DEADLOCK MECHANISM (complete): stale mark (Step 3 gap) -> hides loss from hard-stop/SL -> position ages to 96h -> force_exit claims it (outranking SL, so A.5's mark-refresh branch is unreachable) -> SELL priced at stale anchor -> gateway walks real bids, VWAP == truth -> paper guard measures truth against fiction, sees >10% 'slippage', rejects -> slippage backoff (max 15 min) -> identical retry, forever. Every escape hatch is coincidental: market resolves (price pins -> WI-6), a trade prints within 300s of a scan (RTDS overlay fixes the mark), or bids rally to within 10% of the anchor. CORRECT DESIGN: (1) price exits off the live bid the bot already fetches (fixes paper AND the analogous live FOK no-fill loop — a live SELL limit 0.68 vs bid 0.31 also never fills); (2) in the paper engine, exempt risk-reducing SELLs (or at minimum force_exit/hard_stop reasons, available in event_data) from the adverse guard and fill at bid-walk VWAP — that IS the realistic execution the engine claims to model; a live forced liquidation takes what the book gives; (3) failing both, escalate after N slippage rejects to a re-anchored order instead of Groundhog-Day retries.
